record.paper_title: Three open problems in function theoretic operator theory
record.original_question: Let A be an n by n complex matrix. Let W(A) = {<Ax, x> : x is in C^n and ||x|| = 1} be the numerical range of A, and for a complex polynomial p let ||p(A)|| be the operator norm of p(A). Is it always true that ||p(A)|| <= 2 max{|p(z)| : z is in W(A)}? Equivalently, does the constant-2 numerical-range functional calculus bound hold for every complex matrix and every complex polynomial?

evidence.quote: The numerical range of A, also called the field of values, is denoted by W(A)
Thus, the Crouzeix conjecture was born. Conjecture 2.2 (Crouzeix's conjecture).
At the time of this writing this remains the best constant.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$. Define the numerical range (field of values) of $A$ by
$$W(A) = \{\langle Ax, x\rangle : x \in \mathbb{C}^n, \ \|x\| = 1\},$$
where $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the standard Hermitian inner product on $\mathbb{C}^n$ and $\|\cdot\|$ is the associated Euclidean norm. For a polynomial $p \in \mathbb{C}[z]$, let $\|p(A)\|$ denote the operator (spectral) norm of $p(A)$ acting on $(\mathbb{C}^n, \|\cdot\|)$, and let
$$\|p\|_{W(A)} = \sup\{|p(z)| : z \in W(A)\}.$$
Decide whether the inequality
$$\|p(A)\| \le 2\,\|p\|_{W(A)}$$
holds for every positive integer $n$, every matrix $A \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$, and every polynomial $p \in \mathbb{C}[z]$.
artifact.category_tag: Crouzeix's conjecture / numerical range functional calculus
artifact.status_search_result: Crouzeix's conjecture (the constant 2 bound) remains open as of 2026. It is known to hold in many special cases (normal matrices, 2×2 and 3×3 matrices, near-Jordan blocks, certain tridiagonal and Toeplitz classes), and the best known universal constant is $1+\sqrt{2}$ due to Crouzeix and Palencia (2017). Ongoing workshops and publications continue to treat it as an unresolved problem.

status_evidence.snippet: Despite compelling numerical evidence, no proof has yet been found that the constant equals 2; the best known universal constant is 1+√2.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is still open; best known constant is 1+√2.
